title: Arizona Chip Journey
subtitle: How a chip takes shape in Arizona.
html:
Open Arizona Chip Journey ↗

Project overview

Coming from a business and supply chain background, I started Arizona Chip Journey to prepare for a career in semiconductor sales and account management. Working from public sources, I studied manufacturing processes, materials, equipment, and the surrounding supply chain, then organized what I learned into an interactive site.

What I learned

I completed an upstream wafer preparation introduction and six manufacturing chapters. They gave me a foundation in the process from wafer preparation through front-end fabrication, advanced packaging, and final test, and helped me understand the roles of material suppliers, equipment makers, and chip manufacturers.

Learning the semiconductor industry from the ground up

While looking for work in the United States, I became interested in semiconductor account management. I wanted to understand customers’ manufacturing processes, where their products are used, and the business implications of their technical requirements. Building the site gave me a way to organize what I was learning.

Building a foundation in semiconductor manufacturing

The upstream introduction follows polysilicon, crystal growth, slicing, polishing, and inspection before the wafer enters the fab.

  • Wafer start and surface preparation
  • Patterning and layer transfer
  • Device formation
  • Contacts and interconnect
  • Wafer test and yield
  • Advanced packaging and final test

For each chapter, I looked at process principles, materials, equipment functions, representative suppliers, and their presence in Arizona using traceable public sources. I also studied cross-stage support, including water, industrial gases, chemicals, facility engineering, and logistics.

Connecting technical knowledge to business

My goal was to understand how technology, products, customer needs, and suppliers relate from a business and supply chain perspective. Arizona Chip Journey, Arizona Innovation Map, and Ecosystem Network helped me study the industry through manufacturing, geography, and the wider ecosystem. This is part of how I prepared to enter the semiconductor industry.
